title: ER markers stay on their runs: the core keeps each end straight as long as its marker

v:
## Context

Follow-up to `01M4VNEEYAHMFDVRAB4XSAHKCB` (ER diagram on ELK). The ER renderer draws each cardinality as a `<marker>` attached by its tip at the box (`refX = markerWidth`, ADR-0004: every glyph outside the box) and turned along the route's end segment (`orient="auto-start-reverse"`). How far each marker reaches out along the line, from the glyph farthest from the box: exactly one 15px, zero or one 27px, one or more 42px, zero or more 54px. ELK's runs between a box and the first bend are 20px on the root and 30px in a cluster (half of `spacing.baseValue`, and `CLUSTER_OPTIONS`' `edgeNodeBetweenLayers`), a self-loop's 20px on the root and 12px in a cluster (`spacing.nodeSelfLoop`), and the `rounded` curve cuts 7.07px off each right-angled corner (`cornerCut`, radius 5). So a crow's foot regularly reached past the bend and stuck out off the line: on the ER parity fixture `er-subgraphs`, 6 of 14 ends (the self-relationship's straight part was 8px against markers of 27 and 54).

What Mermaid 12.2.0 does, read in its dist (`node_modules/.pnpm/mermaid@12.2.0/node_modules/mermaid/dist/chunks/mermaid.esm/`) and measured in headless Chrome:

- **Markers.** `chunk-RLXJHMIZ.mjs` lines 1139-1162 (`only_one`, `zero_or_one`, `one_or_more`, `zero_or_more`) and 1163-1199 (the `_neo` variants, which an ER diagram is drawn with: `markerUnits="userSpaceOnUse"`, `stroke-width="2"`). Separate start and end markers, `orient="auto"`. Reach outside the box (refX to the farthest glyph): only one 15 (`refX` 18, bars at 3 and 9); zero or one 27 (`refX` 30, circle `cx` 9 `r` 6); one or more 24 (`refX` 27, bar at 3, the almond from 9 to 45, so half of it, 18px, is inside the box); zero or more 34 (`refX` 39, circle `cx` 11 `r` 6, the almond from 21 to 57, half inside). The start markers mirror these (`refX` 0 or 18).
- **End runs.** On the four ER parity fixtures and a self-relationship document, Mermaid's routes are ELK's, drawn `rounded`: the straight part of a first or last run (from the box to where the corner's curve starts) is 12.9px on most bent ends (a 20px run less the 7.07px corner), 6px on a self-relationship (`er-subgraphs`' `MEMBER |o--o{ MEMBER`: 238.2 to 232.2, then the corner), and the whole route where it is straight. Against markers reaching 15 to 34px, **Mermaid's own markers overrun the bend** on most bent ends, the self-relationship's by 21 and 28px.

So matching Mermaid's marker size and placement alone would not keep the markers on their runs: even its 15px "only one" overruns a 12.9px straight part.

## Decision

The layout core keeps each end straight for as long as the marker on it, a departure from Mermaid 12 recorded here under rule 1 of `01M4VANRC6B2C14NHVC2KRZ9Y8`. The marker figure and pixel counts stay ADR-0004's.

- `DirectedGraphEdge.straightEnds: { start, end }` (core): how far the route must run straight out of each box before its first bend, past the rounding. The ER adapter fills it from `CARDINALITY_MARKER_REACH` (15 / 27 / 42 / 54, the renderer's glyphs), alongside `cornerRadius`.
- The core honours it through ELK, before layout (`holdStraightEnds`): each graph (root or cluster) directly holding a box an edge ends at takes `elk.layered.spacing.edgeNodeBetweenLayers` of at least that end's length plus `cornerRadius × √2`; a box with a self-loop takes `elk.spacing.nodeSelfLoop` of at least that through `elk.spacing.individual`. Neither is lowered below the graph's own; an input without `straightEnds` (every other kind) is laid out exactly as before. Measured with elkjs 0.9.3: `edgeNodeBetweenLayers` is read per graph only (an individual per-box value is ignored), `nodeSelfLoop` per box through `elk.spacing.individual`, and `spacing.edgeNode` changes neither run.
- No geometry is adjusted after ELK and none in the adapter (rule 2).

Rejected: a post-layout pass sliding the bend along the run. Between a box and its relationship's label the room is often shorter than the marker (on a TB stack, 48px under a box against a 61px requirement), so the bend would have had to cross the label or the next box.

## Evidence

The render test (`renderErDiagramToSVG.test.ts`, "render() keeps every cardinality marker on its relationship's end run") reads each drawn marker's reach and each route's `data-siren-points` and requires the straight part of every first and last run, after `cornerCut`, to be at least the reach; over `er-subgraphs`, a self-relationship document and every cardinality in TB and LR it failed on 16 ends before and passes on all after.

Parity, the four ER fixtures against Mermaid 12.2.0 (headless Chrome): crossings 0 against 0, through unrelated boxes 0, vertical 97.2%, horizontal 100%, failures 0, through titles 1 (was 2; Mermaid 2) — unchanged but for the title. Flowchart (176 / 176, 99.6% / 97.8%, through titles 15), class (0 / 0, 97.3% / 100%) and state (0 / 0, 100% / 98.5%) unchanged.

## Consequences

ER pictures are larger along the rank axis where a long marker sits: the span of the boxes grows from 315×1271 to 340×1622 on `er-subgraphs` (Mermaid 280×1321), from 1623×244 to 1797×244 on `example-er-core` (LR; Mermaid 1439×264), from 1212×335 to 1212×418 on `er-long-labels`; `example-er-reveal` (straight routes) is unchanged. Self-loops reach out as far as their longer marker plus 7px. Adopting Mermaid's half-buried almond (reach 24 and 34 instead of 42 and 54) would shorten the floor to 41px; that would change ADR-0004's marker design and is left open.
